name: Hitomi
summary: Short-lived Japanese X-ray mission that, despite limited initial observations, provided an important test of the 3.5 keV dark-matter-line hypothesis through high-resolution Perseus spectra.
detection_principle: Cryogenic microcalorimeters measure photon energy through the tiny temperature rise from single-photon absorption, resolving thermal-plasma atomic lines and candidate dark-matter lines.

status.label: Data taking ended / historical experiment
status.evidence: Contact lost on 2016-03-27; recovery efforts ended on April 28.

results.summary: Constrained the 3.5 keV line strength in a specific Perseus region; this cannot be generalized to exclusion of all dark-matter models.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
